chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Tamim ibn Tarafah
That two men recognized a camel, so each of them presented evidence, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) divided it between them.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.عَرَفَا: recognized (claimed ownership based on knowledge of the animal's traits)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve a dispute when two men both claimed the same camel with evidence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) pragmatic judicial approach in *Tahdhib*, where he resolved a dispute over a lost camel (*ba'ir*) by dividing it when two witnesses presented equal claims. This case exemplifies the Shia legal principle of *qara'ah* (drawing lots) or equitable division when evidence is balanced, reflecting the Imam’s wisdom in maintaining social harmony through fair distribution rather than rigid adjudication.
